cves: Admidio from 5.0.0 before 5.0.16 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in ForumService::saveTopic() that allows authenticated members to modify other users' forum topics. Attackers can replace the topic_uuid parameter in their own topic_save request, reusing their CSRF token, to overwrite the victim topic's title and first post.

Admidio from 5.0.11 before 5.0.16 contains a broken access control vulnerability in modules/inventory/inventory_data.php that allows authenticated users to bypass the inventory_module_enabled restriction. Attackers with any valid login can request the DataTables JSON feed to read every inventory item and keeper names, even when the module is disabled.

Admidio 4.3.2 through 4.3.17 and 5.0.0 before 5.0.15 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows role administrators to assign users to roles in other organizations. Attackers can submit crafted assign requests to members_assignment.php with a foreign role UUID to gain privileged membership, log into that organization, and edit its user profiles.

Admidio before 5.0.12 fails to enforce login-only module restrictions in RSS feed endpoints for forum and announcements modules. Unauthenticated attackers can retrieve forum topics and announcements by sending GET requests to rss/forum.php or rss/announcements.php, disclosing titles, full post text, author names, and timestamps.

Admidio before 5.0.12 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in the relation_type_list parameter of lists_show.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary SQL queries. Attackers can bypass authentication by providing a dummy UUID in role_list and inject SQL through relation_type_list to extract database contents including password hashes and user credentials.

The access control logic in modules/forum.php fails to validate the login-only configuration state, allowing unauthenticated attackers to read forum topics and posts by directly accessing the module with read-only parameters.
